description:
You have a Java project called 'ModularApp' open in Eclipse IDE. The project contains four packages:

- com.appcore.api — Contains HttpApiClient.java which uses java.net.http.HttpClient, HttpRequest, and HttpResponse
- com.appcore.model — Contains User.java, a plain data model class with no external module dependencies
- com.appcore.data — Contains DatabaseConfig.java which uses java.sql.Connection and java.sql.DriverManager
- com.appcore.logging — Contains AppLogger.java which uses java.util.logging.Logger and java.util.logging.Level

The project currently has NO module-info.java file. Your task is to create a proper Java Platform Module System (JPMS) module descriptor.

Create a file 'module-info.java' in the project's source folder (src/) with the following requirements:

1. Module name: com.appcore
2. Required modules:
   - java.net.http (needed by the API package)
   - java.sql (needed by the data package)
   - java.logging (needed by the logging package)
3. Exported packages (public API only):
   - com.appcore.api
   - com.appcore.model
4. Do NOT export internal implementation packages:
   - com.appcore.data (internal)
   - com.appcore.logging (internal)

Ensure the project compiles successfully after adding the module descriptor.

Finally, save a summary to /home/ga/module_report.txt with exactly 3 lines:
- Line 1: The module name
- Line 2: Comma-separated list of required modules in alphabetical order (e.g., java.logging, java.net.http, java.sql)
- Line 3: Comma-separated list of exported packages in alphabetical order (e.g., com.appcore.api, com.appcore.model)
